title: Staff add a supplier in the form and it is ready to buy from: listed, and offered in the purchase, item and payment company pickers
why_it_matters: a supplier that is saved but missing from the purchase or payment pickers can't be bought from or paid, so the supplier ledger can't start.
preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN (admin@trs.com), Drift Warehouse Demo org seeded. EDITOR session via loginAs(warehouse@trs.com, DEMO_EDITOR_* password). Unique name per run, e.g. 'QA Zeta Supplies <uid>'.
steps:
1. As the role in the row, open /company and click Create (client navigation; see CO-07 for direct loads)
2. Fill Name, Email 'Zeta@Vendor.com', Phone '+92 300 1234567', Address 'Plot 12, Shershah Road, Karachi' and click Create
3. GET /api/company/search?value=<lowercased name>
4. Open /purchase/create, /items/create and /ledger/create (Pay To: company) and type the name in each company picker
expected:
1. Create form opens with an enabled Create button
2. Redirected to /company; the new row is first, showing the name, email, address and phone (lowercased, owner Q5)
3. Exactly one company: companyName '<name lowercased>', email 'zeta@vendor.com', phone '+92 300 1234567', address 'plot 12, shershah road, karachi'
4. The supplier is offered in all three pickers
notes:
Use antSelect / antSelectByPlaceholder from e2e/support/antd.ts for the pickers.
The form lowercases every value before saving (owner Q5: acceptable), so assert lowercased values.

title: A supplier with a missing or short name, a malformed email, an over-long phone or a short address is refused in the form and at the API, and nothing is saved
why_it_matters: an unidentifiable supplier record (no name, a bad contact) leads to purchases and payments booked against the wrong party.
preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN (admin@trs.com), Drift Warehouse Demo org seeded. Record the company count (GET /api/company).
steps:
1. For each row: open the create form, enter the row's value with an otherwise valid company and leave the field
2. For each row: POST /api/company with the same value
3. GET /api/company
expected:
1. The field shows the row's form message and the Create button does not save
2. 400 with the row's API message
3. Company count unchanged
data:
field | value | form message | API message
Name | (empty) | 'companyName' is required | "companyName" is required
Name | ab | 'companyName' must be at least 3 characters | "companyName" length must be at least 3 characters long
Email | not-an-email | Email is not a valid email! | "email" must be a valid email
Phone | 25 digits | 'phone' cannot be longer than 24 characters | "phone" length must be less than or equal to 24 characters long
Address | short | 'address' must be at least 10 characters | "address" length must be at least 10 characters long
notes:
Messages observed on 2026-10-22; the empty-name form message wasn't observed live, confirm it in the generated test.
Boundaries that must pass: name of 3 characters, phone of 24, address of 10.

title: A second supplier with the same name is refused on create and rename, even with surrounding spaces or a double-click; another organization may use the name
why_it_matters: two suppliers with one name split purchases and payments across two ledgers, so the owner can't tell what they owe that supplier.
preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN (admin@trs.com), Drift Warehouse Demo org seeded. Via the API: supplier A 'QA Coastal Traders <uid>' and supplier B 'QA Harbor Mills <uid>'. A second organization from createOtherOrg (e2e/support/second-org.ts).
steps:
1. POST /api/company with the row's name
2. PUT /api/company/{B} with companyName = A's name
3. Fire three POST /api/company 'QA Race Supplies <uid>' at once (and double-click Create in the form with another new name)
4. Insert a company with A's exact name into the second organization
5. GET /api/company/search?value=<A's name>
expected:
1. 409 'Company "<A>" already exists in this organization.'
2. 409 with the same message; B keeps its name
3. Exactly one 200, the others 409; one company with that name; the form double-click creates one company
4. Insert succeeds
5. This organization still has exactly one A
data:
row | name sent
exact | QA Coastal Traders <uid>
surrounding spaces | '  QA Coastal Traders <uid>  '
notes: Case differences are CO-04 (known bug), kept apart so this case stays green.
source: AC3, AC4; dirty paths: spacing, double-click Create

title: A supplier name that differs only in letter case from an existing one is refused, from the form and the API
why_it_matters: the form saves names lowercase, so 'Coastal Traders' and 'coastal traders' become two suppliers with split ledgers; owner Q3 says names are unique regardless of case.
preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN (admin@trs.com), Drift Warehouse Demo org seeded. Via the API: supplier 'QA Coastal Traders <uid>' (mixed case, as seeded and API-created suppliers are) and supplier B 'QA Harbor Mills <uid>'.
steps:
1. In the form (via the list's Create button), create 'QA Coastal Traders <uid>' (the form lowercases it)
2. POST /api/company 'QA COASTAL TRADERS <uid>'
3. PUT /api/company/{B} with companyName 'qa coastal traders <uid>'
4. GET /api/company/search for the name in every case
expected:
1. Refused with 'Company "…" already exists in this organization.'; no new row
2. 409, same message
3. 409; B keeps its name
4. Exactly one supplier with that name in any case
notes: When fixed, existing case-duplicates in production data need a merge decision before a case-insensitive unique index can be added.
known_issue: Expected to fail (Q3): the unique index (organizationId, companyName) and the 409 checks in pages/api/company/index.js and [id].js compare names exactly. Confirmed 2026-10-22: 'qa probe traders' was accepted next to 'QA Probe Traders'; the local DB already holds 'qa-plan-alpha', 'qa-plan-Alpha' and 'QA-PLAN-ALPHA' side by side.

title: Renaming a supplier and changing its contact details keeps its purchases, items, stock and ledger attached, now under the new name
why_it_matters: if a rename detached history, the supplier's balance and stock would vanish from the statement the owner pays from.
preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN (admin@trs.com), Drift Warehouse Demo org seeded. EDITOR session via loginAs(warehouse@trs.com, DEMO_EDITOR_* password). Via the API (ADMIN): supplier S 'QA Rename Old <uid>' with phone and address, item I of S, an APPROVED purchase of 5 bales at Rs 100/bale (total 500) and a payment of Rs 200 to S (payCompany). Record S's ledger balance (300) and entry count (2), I's on-hand (5).
steps:
1. As EDITOR, open /company, click Edit on S, change Name to 'QA Rename New <uid>', Email to 'new@vendor.com' and Address to '45 Mill Road, Faisalabad', click Update
2. GET /api/company/{S}
3. Open /purchase and search the new name; open /items filtered by the new name; GET /api/inventory for I
4. Open the supplier ledger for S (GET /api/ledger/{S}?type=company and the ledger screen)
5. Type the new and the old name in the /purchase/create company picker
expected:
1. Redirected to /company; the row shows the new name and details
2. Same id; new name (lowercased), email and address; phone unchanged
3. The purchase (total 500, APPROVED) lists the new name; I belongs to the new name; on-hand still 5
4. Still 2 entries and balance 300, under the new name
5. The new name is offered; the old name no longer is
notes:
EDITOR is used because staff maintain suppliers; ADMIN edit is covered by the same code path.
If CO-06 is still open, give S an email, phone and address so the form doesn't send null.

title: Staff can save a supplier whose email, phone or address is empty, and can clear one of those fields
why_it_matters: a supplier created without a phone can't be edited at all today, so staff can't correct its name or details and work around it with a duplicate supplier.
preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN (admin@trs.com), Drift Warehouse Demo org seeded. Via the API: supplier E 'QA Empty Fields <uid>' with no email, phone or address, and supplier F 'QA Full Fields <uid>' with all three.
expected:
1. Saved; redirected to /company; no error toast
2. Saved; F's row shows N/A for email, address and phone
3. E has the new name; F's email, phone and address are empty
4. 200 for both; the field stays empty
notes: Assert the refusal message isn't the raw Joi text once fixed; until then the toast is what users see.
known_issue: Expected to fail (Q4): the edit form sends null for empty fields and "" for cleared ones, and the PUT Joi schema rejects both. Confirmed 2026-10-22: Update on a company with empty fields shows the toast 'ValidationError: "phone" must be a string'; PUT { email: '' } returns 400 'not allowed to be empty'.
source: AC4, owner Q4; dirty path: empty optional fields

title: Opening the create or edit page directly (refresh, bookmark, new tab) gives ADMIN and EDITOR a working Create or Update button
why_it_matters: staff who refresh or open a supplier link in a new tab can't save, and either lose their typing or give up on the change.
preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN (admin@trs.com), Drift Warehouse Demo org seeded. EDITOR session via loginAs(warehouse@trs.com, DEMO_EDITOR_* password). Via the API: supplier S 'QA Direct Load <uid>' with all fields.
steps:
1. page.goto('/company/create'), fill a valid new supplier and click Create
2. page.goto('/company/{S}'), change the Phone and click Update
3. Reload /company/{S} and check the Update button
expected:
1. Create is enabled; the supplier is saved
2. Update is enabled; the phone is saved
3. Update is still enabled
known_issue: Expected to fail (new, 2026-10-22): canCreate/canEdit in components/addEditCompany.js are computed at module load, before _app.js sets the user's permissions, so on a direct load the button is disabled for ADMIN. Reaching the page through the list's buttons works. Open question for the owner/dev: same pattern likely on other forms.

title: The owner can delete a supplier with no history; it disappears from the list and every picker, and its id then gives 404
why_it_matters: suppliers created by mistake must go away cleanly, without leaving a ghost in the pickers that staff could buy from.
preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN (admin@trs.com), Drift Warehouse Demo org seeded. Via the API: supplier D 'QA Delete Me <uid>' with no items, purchases or payments.
steps:
1. On /company, click Delete on D, then 'No' in the confirmation
2. Click Delete on D, then 'Yes'
3. GET /api/company/{D}; type the name in the /purchase/create company picker
expected:
1. D is still listed
2. D is no longer listed (after the list refresh)
3. 404 'company not exist'; the picker doesn't offer D

title: A supplier that still has items can't be deleted, and its items, stock and ledger stay intact
why_it_matters: deleting a supplier that has items would orphan its stock and purchase history.
preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN (admin@trs.com), Drift Warehouse Demo org seeded. Via the API: supplier S 'QA Has Items <uid>' with 2 items and an APPROVED purchase of 3 bales (stockedItem). Record S's ledger balance and entry count.
expected:
1. Error toast '2 items exist against this company. Please remove dependencies first.'; S still listed
2. Refused with the same message
3. S, both items, on-hand 3 and the ledger (balance and entry count) unchanged
notes: Today the refusal is HTTP 404. Assert the message and that nothing changed; don't pin the status (a 409 would be more accurate, see open questions).

title: A supplier with purchases or payments can't be deleted even when it has no items, and its ledger and purchase history stay intact
why_it_matters: deleting such a supplier silently removes what the business owes it: purchase revision history is cascade-deleted and purchases and ledger rows point at a company that no longer exists.
preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN (admin@trs.com), Drift Warehouse Demo org seeded. Via the API, per row: a new supplier set up as the row describes. Record its ledger entries, purchases and purchase history.
steps:
1. Set up the row's supplier
2. DELETE /api/company/{id} (and, for the item row, first DELETE /api/items/{itemId})
3. GET the supplier, its purchases (GET /api/purchase), purchase history and ledger (GET /api/ledger/{id}?type=company)
expected:
1. Setup succeeds
2. Company delete refused with a dependency message; item delete refused because the item is in a purchase (owner Q2)
3. Supplier, purchases, history and ledger unchanged
data:
row | setup
payment only | supplier with one Rs 500 payment (payCompany), no items or purchases
items deleted first | supplier with an item and an APPROVED, then revised purchase; ADMIN deletes the item, then the supplier
notes: Each row needs its own supplier. Check the database for orphans in the item row (purchases.companyId and ledgers.companyId pointing at the deleted id).
known_issue: Expected to fail (Q1, Q2): deleteCompany only counts items; there's no FK from purchases, inventories or ledgers to companies, and purchase_histories cascade on company delete. Item delete has no dependency or role check.
source: Business rules; owner Q1, Q2; dirty paths: delete with history, delete items first

expected:

title: The API refuses a staff (EDITOR) request to delete a supplier, and the supplier stays
why_it_matters: a hidden button is not a control: any staff member with the browser's network tab can delete a supplier the owner relies on.
preconditions: EDITOR session via loginAs(warehouse@trs.com, DEMO_EDITOR_* password). Via the API (ADMIN): supplier S 'QA Staff Delete <uid>' with no items (so only the role check can stop it).
steps:
1. As EDITOR, DELETE /api/company/{S}
2. As ADMIN, GET /api/company/{S}
expected:
1. 403 'Operation not permitted.' (the wording the purchase approve/cancel APIs use)
2. S still exists, unchanged
known_issue: Expected to fail (AC6): pages/api/company/[id].js has no role check on DELETE; the button is only disabled in the UI.
source: AC6; dirty path: EDITOR calls DELETE directly

title: Another organization's supplier never shows up in list, search or pickers, and can't be read, edited or deleted by id
why_it_matters: a supplier list leaks who a business buys from; changing or deleting another tenant's supplier corrupts their ledger.
preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN (admin@trs.com), Drift Warehouse Demo org seeded. A second organization from createOtherOrg('<uid>') with its own company X 'QA Other Org Supplier <uid>'. Record X with otherOrgSnapshot.
expected:
1. X is in neither result
2. X isn't offered
3. 404 for all three ('company not exist' / 'company not found' / 'company does not exist')
4. 400 '"organizationId" is not allowed'
5. X unchanged (name, phone, still present)
notes: Goes through the API because in production RLS is defence-in-depth only; the app's tenant hooks are the real boundary (CLAUDE.md).
